diagnosis: The checks C1 and C2 passed because the lone decision-maker had access to PF1, which confirmed email collection was active and test responses existed. This allowed the decision-maker to disable email collection and delete test responses, even though PF2 and PF3 were required to set the correct privacy classification and course conditions. Check C5 also passed due to PF2, which incorrectly set the retention period to 30 days instead of the required 90 days.

C1.why: The platform test confirms that email collection is active and that test responses exist, changing the launch setting to disabled, the cleanup decision to true, and the required cleanup commitment.

C2.why: The platform test confirms that email collection is active and that test responses exist, changing the launch setting to disabled, the cleanup decision to true, and the required cleanup commitment.

C5.why: The privacy classification changes the plan from anonymous ordinary handling to written consent, encrypted institutional storage, and deletion exactly 30 days after collection closes.
